firing.source:
import { useState } from 'react';
export const value = 1;

findings.message: This imports a name out of react directly. Reach it through the React namespace instead. A bare `useState` or `Ref` at a call site says nothing about where it came from, so a reader has to go to the import block to find out, and a local binding with the same name shadows it silently. React.useState carries its provenance with it.

This import takes names out of react without importing React itself, so there is no namespace to reach through and every use in the file has to be a bare name. Import React as the default and use React.* instead.
